reason: Extend structured simulation to 49 previously unmapped occupations and directly bind ten technology activity options. Preserve all original profiles, official answers, previous career bindings, scoring, support gates, salary/education ranking and first-three Top definition. Review development cases first; freeze before additional holdout evaluation.
limitations: Bindings are authored test assumptions, not learned weights or independent validation.

Unmapped or unstated specialist preferences remain unfamiliar; unknown official 60-item responses use neutral 3 and are explicitly marked as simulation conventions. Positive official responses use Like (4), negative responses Dislike (2), with no invented intensity.
Original 172 profiles retain their existing structured answers and provenance; original data is not rewritten.

200 additional holdouts were assigned before outcome runs and receive no case-specific edits. Earlier aggregate results have been seen, so this is not an untouched final validation set. Original 30 and fresh 12 holdouts remain separately identified.
Historical failed policies are preserved in research only; no historical word classifier is imported in the release pipeline.
Ten technology activity options have direct authored bindings; all prior option assumptions outside these ten are frozen rather than recomputed from the enlarged career map.
23 development profiles gaining a first Top received author narrative review. Other changed pairs and holdout cases still need independent qualitative review.
Some specific supported interests conflict with broad RIASEC correlation. Values remain visible; no correlation or support threshold changed.
